title: Ethiopian Minced Meat Sauce
community: All of Ethiopia — the minced meat sauce for everyday eating
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Minchet Abish — seasoned minced beef cooked with berbere, kibbeh, onions, tomatoes, and a touch of niter kibbeh into a thick, richly spiced meat sauce eaten with injera or ayib. Ethiopia's everyday minced meat dish — less ceremonial than kitfo, more accessible, deeply satisfying.
longDesc: Minchet Abish is the everyday minced beef dish of Ethiopia — cooked through (unlike kitfo), sauced (unlike tibs), and deeply spiced with berbere. It is the weekday version of the celebration dishes — completely satisfying and far simpler to prepare.
steps: Add kibbeh. Add berbere. Toast 2 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, tomato paste, and tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes.
Add minced beef. Break up. Brown thoroughly — 8 minutes.
Add water. Simmer 20 minutes until thick.
chefTips: Break the mince up thoroughly — no lumps.
The sauce should be thick enough to scoop with injera.
cookingScience: See ETH026 for Key Wat cooking science. The difference with Minchet Abish is the surface area — minced beef has dramatically more surface area than cubed beef, so the Maillard reaction occurs much faster and the berbere permeates the meat more rapidly.
sustainabilityTips: Minced beef uses less premium cuts — more sustainable use of the whole animal.
servedWith: As part of a combination platter
culturalNote: Minchet Abish is the weekday workhorse of Ethiopian cooking — prepared quickly, deeply satisfying, and eaten by everyone from students to elders. It is the dish that makes injera irresistible even on the plainest day.
